variants.title: CSDA range of 100 MeV protons in silver (Bethe-Bloch)
variants.unknown: the range of 100 MeV protons in silver
variants.note: Fewer electrons per gram and a larger mean excitation energy than carbon: the range in g/cm² is about half as long again, and the dense metal makes it far shorter in centimetres.

source.title: PDG 'Atomic and nuclear properties of materials' / ICRU Reports 37 and 49: Z/A, mean excitation energy I, density

variants.title: CSDA range of 100 MeV protons in gold (Bethe-Bloch)
variants.unknown: the range of 100 MeV protons in gold
variants.note: Gold's inner electrons are tightly bound (I = 790 eV), so the uncorrected formula is less accurate here than in light media; the shell correction this program leaves out matters most at the low-energy end.

source.title: PDG 'Atomic and nuclear properties of materials' / ICRU Reports 37 and 49: Z/A, mean excitation energy I, density

variants.title: CSDA range of 100 MeV protons in lead (Bethe-Bloch)
variants.unknown: the range of 100 MeV protons in lead
variants.note: Lead has the fewest electrons per gram of the four media and the largest I, so it has the longest range in g/cm², though it is still about a centimetre and a half of metal.

source.title: PDG 'Atomic and nuclear properties of materials' / ICRU Reports 37 and 49: Z/A, mean excitation energy I, density
